Let <MATH_0001> be a category.
Let <MATH_0002> be a fibred category.
Let <MATH_0003> be the subcategory of <MATH_0004> defined
as follows
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> <MATH_0005>, and
<STRUCT_0003> for <MATH_0006> the set of morphisms between <MATH_0007>
and <MATH_0008> in <MATH_0009> is the set of strongly cartesian morphisms between
<MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> in <MATH_0012>.
<STRUCT_0004>
Let <MATH_0013> be the restriction of <MATH_0014>
to <MATH_0015>. Then <MATH_0016> is fibred
in groupoids.

Note that the construction makes sense since by
Lemma <REF_0001>
the identity morphism of any object of <MATH_0001> is strongly cartesian,
and the composition of strongly cartesian morphisms is strongly cartesian.
The first lifting property of
Definition <REF_0002>
follows from the condition that in a fibred category
given any morphism <MATH_0002> and <MATH_0003> lying over <MATH_0004> there exists
a strongly cartesian morphism <MATH_0005> lying over <MATH_0006>.
Let us check the second lifting property of
Definition <REF_0003>
for the category <MATH_0007> over <MATH_0008>.
To do this we argue as in the discussion following
Definition <REF_0004>.
Thus in Diagram <REF_0005> the
morphisms <MATH_0009>, <MATH_0010> and <MATH_0011> are strongly cartesian morphisms
of <MATH_0012>.
Hence <MATH_0013> and <MATH_0014> are strongly cartesian morphisms
of <MATH_0015> lying over the same arrow of <MATH_0016> and
having the same target in <MATH_0017>. By the discussion following
Definition <REF_0006>
this means these two arrows are isomorphic as desired (here we use also
that any isomorphism in <MATH_0018> is strongly cartesian, by
Lemma <REF_0007> again).
